hero.title: Jamie Zhang
hero.role: I use vibe coding to turn ideas into web pages.
hero.headline: This is a personal space for my AI tool experiments, project notes, and learning records.
hero.description: I care less about presenting perfect products, and more about making ideas visible enough to test and improve. This site is where I keep the process, not just the final page.
hero.availability: Project notes, drafts, and revisions in one place.
hero.previewDescription: Then keep revising what the page reveals.

work.title: AI tool experiments and web pages.
work.description: The homepage keeps each project short: what it is, why I made it, and what I tried. The details live in the project note pages.

process.title: I usually start by writing the problem clearly.
process.description: My logic training makes me organize materials, constraints, and reasons first. Building the page is only one step; revision and records matter just as much.

steps.title: Clarify
steps.label: CLARIFY
steps.description: Write down the problem, materials, and goal first. I start by organizing the background, needs, and constraints before touching the interface.

steps.title: Build
steps.label: BUILD
steps.description: Use vibe coding to make a live version. The first goal is to make the idea openable, browsable, and easy to revise.

steps.title: Iterate
steps.label: ITERATE
steps.description: Keep adjusting the writing, layout, and interaction. Many problems only become visible after the idea appears on a page.

steps.title: Record
steps.label: RECORD
steps.description: Turn the process into project notes. I document what I made, why I made it, and what still needs work.

about.bio1: I’m Jamie Zhang, a graduate student in logic at China University of Political Science and Law. My background helps me break problems into assumptions, rules, decisions, and conclusions.
about.bio2: Recently, I’ve been using vibe coding to build small web pages and AI tool experiments, then turning the process into project notes. This site is less a polished gallery, and more a personal space for recording what I build, revise, and learn.
